warnings: Lesson is long at 4170 words; consider tightening for reading flow.
Quiz language appears sparse; make assessment prompts explicit.

improvement_notes: Clarify even more explicitly that a range return supports clearance only along the modeled beam, not necessarily throughout the entire endpoint cell; the current wording is careful but the initial definition of “free” could still be read as stronger than the evidence warrants.
Add a compact instructor answer key for the five Mini Simulation predictions, especially the exact qualitative result of the crate visibility and the effect of the diagonal approximation.

State near the beginning of the Python Lab that the simulation operates directly in grid coordinates after the initial position conversion, so beginners do not infer that the ray loop models arbitrary world-frame sensor orientations.

Consider adding one short exercise involving a non-axis-aligned robot heading or an origin offset in both x and y. This would connect the coordinate equations more directly to realistic sensor placement without substantially expanding the lesson.

The lesson is highly complete but somewhat long for a foundational class. Several caveats about uncertainty, endpoint interpretation, and simplified ray traversal could be consolidated into one focused “What the model leaves out” subsection.
